name: Simple CEA/BOTEC of CHAI TSUs, April 2025
summary: Funds technical support units that help governments, such as Malawi's and Burkina Faso's, spend their health budgets better. GiveWell's spreadsheet "Simple CEA/BOTEC of CHAI TSUs, April 2025", linked from 2 of its grant pages. Every number is traced from the sheet's bottom line; calculated rows reproduce the sheet's own values.

rows.label: Likelihood of Scenario 1: Large foundation [anonymized] replaces the full program costs (Burkina Faso)
rows.explainer: We believe there is an unusually high chance that we are funging this large foundation, as it has set up a financing facility with similar objectives to this grant and in countries that overlap with this grant.

rows.label: % improvement in cost-effectivess of government health spending due to allocative efficiencies (Malawi)
rows.explainer: We benchmark this to the 20% improvement to cost-effectiveness that we believe CHAI's GiveWell-funded PPM (Program Performance Management) team can achieve for internal programs. Whilst we believe there may be more room for improvement in the average government program (compared to the average CHAI program), we also think that the cost-effectiveness lense will be weighted less highly in decision making given other government priorities. See the rationale for this PPM grant we made to CHAI in October 2024.

rows.label: Cost-effectiveness of TSU (in multiples of Give Directly's cost-efectiveness, "x cash") (Burkina Faso)
Units of value per dollar given to GiveDirectly
rows.explainer: GiveWell reports this model's result in multiples of cash transfers. Multiplying by GiveWell's value of a dollar to GiveDirectly converts it into units of value per dollar, so it ranks against the other models. Older sheets used older moral weights; the multiple of cash is the comparable number across years.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Default for research, technical assistance and policy work: mostly people. Our judgment; we haven't seen this grant's breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Researchers and advisers could typically earn considerably more in consulting or industry. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest).
